text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In an angry rebuke of Malaysians for their lack of consciousness about cleanliness, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad called for stern action against litterbugs after visiting Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif commented about the rubbish along Jalan Bukit Bintang in Kuala Lumpur.
- Thirteen months after becoming chief minister of northern Kedah state, Sanusi Junid has made a major reshuffle of portfolios among state executive councillors and dropped one member.

- The engineering, procurement and construction contract for the 15 billion ringgit Bakun hydroelectric dam project is not bankable unless it is amended, Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khiing said. He said he is not optimistic the dispute with key contractor ABB Asea Brown Boveri could be resolved by this week.

- In a move to cut speculation on the ringgit and relieve pressure on interest rates, Bank Negara has instructed banks to restrict non-commercial related sales of the local currency to $2 million per foreign customer.

- Bank Negara, in continuing to promote a stable and more predictable environment for genuine investments, has directed banks to observe a $2 million limit on outstanding non-commercial related ringgit offer-side swap transactions with each foreign customer.

- Ericsson Companies in Malaysia said it has always maintained a high standard of business ethics in its relationship with its customers. It made the statement after a Malaysian government probe cleared Ericsson of allegations of irregularities in tenders to Ericsson by Telekom Malaysia.
- The haze has reached such a hazardous level nationwide that the public have been advised to wear masks and refrain from exercising outdoors.
